answers.answer: A hospital group sent a security questionnaire (spreadsheet, 212 questions), due in 12 days. The deal is about $180,000 a year.

answers.answer: We are not SOC 2 certified yet; an audit is booked for next spring.

answers.answer: Written policies for access control and incident response, but not for vendor management.

research.approach: Practitioners treat a security questionnaire as an evidence exercise, not a writing exercise. They triage every question into three honest answers (yes with proof, no with a dated plan, not applicable with a reason), group questions by control area, and confirm what they could actually show before writing a yes. Where a certification is missing, they say so plainly, describe interim controls and give a specific dated milestone rather than a vague promise. They keep a copy of every submission and a master answer library so the next answer stays consistent, and they expect the buyer to verify a handful of answers, usually on encryption, access and incident response. The deal side runs next to the paperwork: someone asks the buyer's security contact early what would be accepted in place of a report.

sources.title: How to respond to a vendor security questionnaire when you don't have everything in place (Decryption Digest)
sources.note: Triage into yes with an evidence path, no with a remediation plan, or N/A with a reason; confirm evidence before a yes; write honest no answers with interim controls and a dated milestone; keep every submission and a master library; buyers often verify three to five answers. Practitioner blog.

sources.title: CSA STAR v4.1 explained: key updates for cloud security and assurance (Cloud Security Alliance)
sources.note: Seen in search results, not opened in full: the CAIQ is the standard cloud-vendor questionnaire; the Level 1 self-assessment is truthful self-reporting and valid for one year. Useful for mapping a custom questionnaire to a common control set.

sources.title: Shared Responsibility Model (Amazon Web Services)
sources.note: AWS secures the cloud infrastructure; the customer secures what it builds and configures on top (data, access settings, encryption choices). AWS Artifact provides AWS's own compliance reports, not ours. Seen in search results, not opened in full; no date seen; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: SOC for service organizations (AICPA & CIMA)
sources.note: SOC reports are CPA-issued examinations of a service organization's controls that help buyers judge outsourcing risk; the page lists exposure drafts for 2027 criteria posted 2026-10-26. It does not itself define Type I and Type II. No date for the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.note: Page blocked fetching (403); seen in search results only. pitfalls.text: Answering yes without an evidence path, or overstating a practice (for example 'monthly scans' when scans are less frequent).
Giving different answers to the same question for different customers, or not keeping a copy of what was submitted.
Vague timelines instead of a dated milestone, or promising a report date the auditor has not confirmed.
Treating AWS's own compliance reports as proof of our controls; they cover AWS's side only.
Citing a policy that is drafted but not adopted as if it were practice.
Missing that the deal may involve patient data and a separate agreement beyond the questionnaire.

hypotheses.statement: Most gaps sit in a few control areas, such as vendor management and the missing SOC 2 report.
hypotheses.test: Count no and in-progress answers by control area from the triage.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 70% of no and in-progress answers fall in four or fewer areas.
hypotheses.refute_if: No answers are spread across more than eight areas with none holding over 20%.

hypotheses.statement: Some written policy statements are not matched by what we do.
hypotheses.test: Check each policy statement a question relies on against the CTO's confirmed controls and proof.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least one statement in ten has no confirmed practice or proof.
hypotheses.refute_if: Every checked statement has confirmed practice and proof.

hypotheses.statement: The buyer will accept a SOC 2 roadmap with interim documents in place of a report.
hypotheses.test: Read the questionnaire for a stated requirement and, if the owner agrees, ask the buyer's security contact what they would accept.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The buyer says in writing that a roadmap, policies and a call are enough, or the questionnaire lists a report as optional.
hypotheses.refute_if: The buyer says in writing that an issued report is required for approval.

hypotheses.statement: The deal puts patient health data in our system, which brings HIPAA duties beyond the questionnaire.
hypotheses.test: Check the questionnaire for HIPAA or business associate questions and ask the owner what customer data the hospital group would send us.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The questionnaire asks for HIPAA safeguards or a business associate agreement, or the owner confirms patient details can appear in support data.
hypotheses.refute_if: The owner confirms no patient data is processed and the questionnaire has no HIPAA section.

hypotheses.statement: A few questions are knock-outs that decide approval on their own.
hypotheses.test: Look for mandatory markings, scoring weights or a minimum bar in the spreadsheet and any covering email.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least one control we lack is marked mandatory or required to pass.
hypotheses.refute_if: Nothing is marked mandatory and no pass mark is stated.

hypotheses.statement: Many questions repeat each other, so one verified answer can cover several.
hypotheses.test: Cluster the 212 questions by meaning and count clusters of two or more.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 40% of questions sit in repeat clusters.

hypotheses.statement: The CTO's time is the bottleneck, not the writing.
hypotheses.test: Count the answers that need a CTO fact or proof and compare with the hours the CTO says are free before day 8.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The CTO-needed items, at about 10 minutes each, exceed the hours the CTO has free.
hypotheses.refute_if: The hours free cover the items with at least 25% to spare.

dropped.reason: The SOC 2 audit is booked for next spring and cannot finish in 12 days; the plan answers 'not certified' honestly instead.

measurement.window: From submission until the buyer gives a written decision; follow-ups logged within one working day.
measurement.min_volume: One deal, so no statistical test; the outcome is the buyer's written response and the list of answers they chose to verify.
measurement.stop_rule: If a follow-up exposes a wrong answer, stop, tell the CTO and the owner, and send a corrected answer with an explanation before any further reply.
